what: Norwegian Cruise Line operates three brands: Norwegian, the upmarket Oceania Cruises and the luxury Regent Seven Seas, sailing worldwide from North American and European ports.
customers: Holidaymakers booking cruises, mostly North Americans, and increasingly affluent ones on the luxury brands.
money: a large part and the better margin
drinks, excursions, casino and shopping on board
moat: Ships cost over a billion dollars each and take years to build, and the shipyards that can build them are full for years ahead, which caps how fast capacity can grow.
risks: $15.9B of debt against $210M of cash, from the pandemic shutdown
Free cash flow is negative because new ships are being paid for
Fuel and port costs are large and outside its control
opportunities: 9.3 times earnings with revenue up from $648M to $9.8B as cruising recovered
Analysts see about 15% upside, with 24 covering the stock
Onboard spending per passenger keeps rising and carries much higher margins than the fare
watch: Net yield per passenger day and progress on reducing debt.
